newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: C. BANK DECIDES ON NEW INSOLVENCY RULES.
newsitem.headline: C. BANK DECIDES ON NEW INSOLVENCY RULES.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank said on Thursday that its board decided on the new rules for when it may declare a commercial bank insolvent.
"The board of the Bank of Lithuania may take a decision to declare a commercial bank insolvent if the net value of its assets is less than the bank's liabilities," the bank said in a statement.
Capital adequacy will be another key factor.
"If the bank's capital adequacy is less than half that required by the regulations of the Bank of Lithuania, which currently stand at 10 percent (it can be declared inslovent)," the statement added.
A bank may also be declared insolvent if it fails to carry out financial obligations to its clients within five days because it lacks funds, the bank said.
The decision will come into affect from July 1, the bank said.
The bank also said that from 1998, taking into consideration the requirements of the European Union, a bank could be declared insolvent if it fails to meet capital adequacy norms.
The country's central bank has committed itself to tightening regulations to avoid a repeat of the crisis which shook the banking sector in late 1995.
